title.zh: 卷350 列傳一百三十七 李长庚子：廷钰 胡振声 王得禄 邱良功 陈步雲 许松年 黄标 林国良 许廷桂
title.en: Volume 350 Biographies 137: Li Changgeng son: Ting Yu, Hu Zhensheng, Wang Delu, Qiu Lianggong, Chen Buyun, Xu Songnian, Huang Biao, Lin Guoliang, Xu Tinggui
title.raw: 卷350 列傳一百三十七 李长庚子：廷钰 胡振声 王得禄 邱良功 陈步雲 许松年 黄标 林国良 许廷桂

sentences.zh: 列傳一百三十七

translations.literal: Biographies 137
translations.idiomatic: Biographies 137

sentences.zh: 李長庚子廷鈺胡振聲王得祿邱良功陳步雲

translations.literal: Li Changgeng, [his son] Ting Yu, Hu Zhensheng, Wang Delu, Qiu Lianggong, Chen Buyun
translations.idiomatic: Li Changgeng, his adopted heir Ting Yu, Hu Zhensheng, Wang Delu, Qiu Lianggong, and Chen Buyun

sentences.zh: 許松年黃標林國良許廷桂

translations.literal: Xu Songnian, Huang Biao, Lin Guoliang, Xu Tinggui
translations.idiomatic: Xu Songnian, Huang Biao, Lin Guoliang, and Xu Tinggui

sentences.zh: 李長庚，字西岩，福建同安人。

translations.literal: Li Changgeng, courtesy name Xiyan, was a native of Tong'an in Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: Li Changgeng, whose courtesy name was Xiyan, came from Tong'an in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 乾隆三十六年武進士，授藍翎侍衛。

translations.literal: In the thirty-sixth year of the Qianlong reign he passed the military metropolitan examination and was appointed an imperial bodyguard with the blue feather insignia.
translations.idiomatic: In 1771 he earned his military jinshi degree and was appointed an imperial bodyguard bearing the blue feather insignia.

sentences.zh: 出為浙江衢州營都司，累遷樂清協副將。

translations.literal: He went out to serve as battalion commander of the Quzhou Garrison in Zhejiang, and was repeatedly promoted to deputy commander of the Yueqing Garrison.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted as battalion commander of the Quzhou Garrison in Zhejiang and rose through successive promotions to deputy commander of the Yueqing Garrison.

sentences.zh: 五十二年，署福建海壇鎮總兵。

translations.literal: In the fifty-second year he acted as regional commander of the Haitan Garrison in Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: In 1787 he served in an acting capacity as regional commander of the Haitan Garrison in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 鄰海有盜，誤指所轄界，坐褫職。

translations.literal: There were pirates in a neighboring maritime jurisdiction; they wrongly identified his command area as where the crime occurred, and he was stripped of office on that charge.
translations.idiomatic: Pirates operating just outside his jurisdiction were wrongly alleged to have struck within his district, and he was dismissed from office on that account.

sentences.zh: 罄家財募鄉勇，捕獲巨盜，起用，補海壇游擊，遷銅山參將。

translations.literal: He exhausted his family wealth to recruit local militia, captured a major pirate, was reinstated, was made up as a battalion officer at Haitan, and was transferred to be brigade commander at Tongshan.
translations.idiomatic: He spent his entire family fortune recruiting local militia, captured a major pirate leader, was reinstated in service, filled a vacancy as battalion officer at Haitan, and was promoted to brigade commander at Tongshan.

sentences.zh: 自乾隆季年，安南內亂，招瀕海亡命劫內洋，以濟餉為患，粵東土盜鳳尾、水澳兩幫附之，遂益肆擾。

translations.literal: From the late Qianlong years Annam was embroiled in civil strife and recruited coastal desperadoes to plunder the inner seas to fund its armies, which became a scourge; the Cantonese land-pirate bands Fengwei and Shuiao attached themselves to them and the disturbances grew worse.
translations.idiomatic: In the closing years of Qianlong's reign civil war in Annam drew desperate men from along the coast to raid China's inner seas for supplies, and the plague worsened when the Guangdong pirate bands Fengwei and Shuiao joined in, making the depredations steadily bolder.

sentences.zh: 五十九年，夷艇始犯福建三澎，長庚擊走之。

translations.literal: In the fifty-ninth year foreign pirate junks first raided the Three Pescadores of Fujian; Changgeng drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: In 1794 foreign pirate junks raided Fujian's Three Pescadores for the first time, and Changgeng repelled them.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶二年，遷澎湖協副將，擢浙江定海鎮總兵。

translations.literal: In the second year of the Jiaqing reign he was transferred to be deputy commander of the Penghu Garrison and was promoted to regional commander of the Dinghai Garrison in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: In 1797 he was made deputy commander of the Penghu Garrison and promoted to regional commander of the Dinghai Garrison in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 三年，迭擊洋匪於衢港及普陀。

translations.literal: In the third year he repeatedly attacked foreign pirates at Qu Port and Putuo.
translations.idiomatic: In 1798 he fought foreign pirates repeatedly at Qu Port and Putuo.

sentences.zh: 四年，鳳尾幫引夷艇入溫州洋，敗之，賜花翎。

translations.literal: In the fourth year the Fengwei gang led foreign junks into the Wenzhou seas; he defeated them and was granted the peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: In 1799 the Fengwei gang brought foreign junks into Wenzhou waters; he defeated them and was awarded the peacock feather insignia.

sentences.zh: 五年夏，夷艇合水澳、鳳尾百餘艘萃於浙洋，逼台州。

translations.literal: In the summer of the fifth year, more than a hundred foreign junks together with the Shuiao and Fengwei gangs gathered in the Zhejiang seas and pressed on Taizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of 1800 more than a hundred foreign junks together with the Shuiao and Fengwei gangs massed in Zhejiang waters and threatened Taizhou.

sentences.zh: 巡撫阮元奏以長庚總統三鎮水師擊之，會師海門。

translations.literal: Grand Coordinator Ruan Yuan memorialized that Changgeng should command the naval forces of the three garrisons to attack them, and the armies united at Haimen.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Coordinator Ruan Yuan petitioned that Changgeng take overall command of the three garrisons' naval forces to strike them, and the fleets rendezvoused at Haimen.

sentences.zh: 賊泊松門山下相持，颶風大作，覆溺幾盡，其泊岸及附敗舟者皆就俘，獲安南偽侯倫貴利等四總兵，磔之，以敕印擲還其國。

translations.literal: The bandits anchored below Songmen Mountain in a standoff; a great typhoon arose and nearly all were capsized and drowned; those who reached shore or clung to wrecked boats were all taken prisoner; four Annamese false marquises including Lun Guili were captured, dismembered, and the imperial patent was thrown back to their country.
translations.idiomatic: The pirates lay at anchor below Songmen Mountain in a stalemate until a violent typhoon struck and nearly all were capsized and drowned; those who reached shore or clung to wreckage were taken prisoner. Four Annamese pretender marquises including Lun Guili were captured, executed by dismemberment, and their imperial patent was cast back toward their country.

sentences.zh: 是年，擢福建水師提督，尋調浙江。

translations.literal: That year he was promoted to naval commander-in-chief of Fujian, and soon was transferred to Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: That year he was promoted to naval commander-in-chief of Fujian and soon transferred to Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 安南烏艚船百餘號，總兵十二人，分前中後三隊，所獲四總兵，其後隊也。

translations.literal: The Annamese had more than a hundred black-painted junks and twelve regional commanders, divided into front, middle, and rear squadrons; the four commanders captured were from the rear squadron.
translations.idiomatic: The Annamese force numbered more than a hundred black-painted junks under twelve regional commanders organized in front, middle, and rear squadrons; the four commanders taken were from the rear squadron.

sentences.zh: 未幾，安南新阮內附，受封守約束，艇匪無所巢穴。

translations.literal: Before long the new Nguyen regime in Annam submitted and accepted investiture under restraint, and the junk pirates had no roost.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the new Nguyen regime in Annam submitted to the Qing and accepted investiture under restraint, leaving the junk pirates without a base.

sentences.zh: 其在閩者，皆為漳盜蔡牽所並，有艇百餘，粵盜硃濆亦得數十艘。

translations.literal: Those remaining in Fujian were all absorbed by the Zhangzhou pirate Cai Qian, who had more than a hundred junks; the Cantonese pirate Zhu Fen also obtained several dozen vessels.
translations.idiomatic: Those still operating in Fujian were absorbed by the Zhangzhou pirate Cai Qian, who commanded more than a hundred junks, while the Cantonese pirate Zhu Fen acquired several dozen vessels of his own.

sentences.zh: 牽，同安人，奸猾善用眾，既得夷艇，凡水澳、鳳尾諸黨悉歸之，遂猖獗。

translations.literal: Qian was a native of Tong'an, cunning and skilled at using his followers; once he obtained foreign junks, all the Shuiao, Fengwei, and other factions submitted to him, and he grew rampant.
translations.idiomatic: Qian came from Tong'an, was cunning and skilled at marshaling men, and once he seized foreign junks every faction from Shuiao and Fengwei onward fell in behind him, after which his raids grew brazen.

sentences.zh: 阮元與長庚議夷艇高大，水師戰艦不能制，乃集捐十餘萬金付長庚，赴閩造大艦三十，名曰霆船，鑄大砲四百餘配之。

translations.literal: Ruan Yuan and Changgeng discussed how the foreign junks were tall and the naval warships could not master them; they therefore raised more than a hundred thousand taels in donations and gave them to Changgeng to go to Fujian and build thirty large ships called Thunder ships, casting more than four hundred great cannon to equip them.
translations.idiomatic: Ruan Yuan and Changgeng agreed that the foreign junks towered too high for existing naval warships to overcome, so they raised more than a hundred thousand taels in donations and sent Changgeng to Fujian to build thirty large vessels called Thunder ships, fitting them with more than four hundred heavy cannon.

sentences.zh: 連敗牽等於海上，軍威大振。

translations.literal: He repeatedly defeated Qian and others at sea, and military prestige rose greatly.
translations.idiomatic: He defeated Qian and his allies again and again at sea, and the navy's prestige soared.

sentences.zh: 八年，牽竄定海，進香普陀山，長庚掩至，牽僅以身免，窮追至閩洋，賊船糧盡帆壞，偽乞降於總督玉德，遣興泉永道慶徠赴三沙招撫，玉德遽檄浙師收港，牽得以其間修船揚帆去。

translations.literal: In the eighth year Qian fled to Dinghai and went to burn incense at Mount Putuo; Changgeng came upon him by surprise and Qian barely escaped with his life; pursued to the Fujian seas, the pirate ships' provisions were exhausted and sails ruined; he falsely begged to surrender to Governor-General Yu De, who sent Xing-Quan-Yong Circuit Intendant Qing Lai to Sansha to offer amnesty; Yu De hastily ordered the Zhejiang fleet to withdraw to port, and Qian used the interval to repair his ships and sail away.
translations.idiomatic: In 1803 Qian slipped into Dinghai and went to offer incense at Mount Putuo; Changgeng surprised him and Qian barely escaped alive. Changgeng pursued him into Fujian waters until the pirate fleet ran out of provisions and its sails were ruined. Qian then feigned surrender to Governor-General Yu De, who sent Circuit Intendant Qing Lai to Sansha to negotiate amnesty and hastily ordered the Zhejiang fleet back to port, giving Qian time to refit his ships and sail away.

sentences.zh: 浙師追擊於三沙及溫州，毀其船六。

translations.literal: The Zhejiang fleet pursued and attacked at Sansha and Wenzhou, destroying six of his ships.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhejiang fleet gave chase at Sansha and Wenzhou and destroyed six of his ships.

sentences.zh: 牽畏霆船，賄閩商造大艇，高於霆船，出洋以被劫報，牽得之，渡橫洋，劫台灣米以餉硃濆，遂與之合。

translations.literal: Qian feared the Thunder ships, bribed Fujian merchants to build large junks taller than the Thunder ships, sent them out to sea reporting that they had been robbed, and obtained them; he crossed the open ocean, plundered Taiwan rice to supply Zhu Fen, and then joined with him.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing the Thunder ships, Qian bribed Fujian merchants to build junks taller than them, sent the vessels to sea under false reports of robbery, and took possession of them. He then crossed the open ocean, raided Taiwan for rice to supply Zhu Fen, and joined forces with him.

sentences.zh: 九年夏，連宗八十餘入閩，戕總兵胡振聲，詔治閩將不援罪，長庚總統兩省水師。

translations.literal: In the summer of the ninth year more than eighty vessels of the Lian clan entered Fujian and killed Regional Commander Hu Zhensheng; an edict punished the Fujian officers for failing to reinforce, and Changgeng took overall command of the naval forces of the two provinces.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of 1804 more than eighty vessels of the Lian clan entered Fujian and killed Regional Commander Hu Zhensheng. An edict punished Fujian officers for failing to reinforce, and Changgeng was placed in overall command of the two provinces' naval forces.

sentences.zh: 秋，牽、濆共犯浙，長庚合諸鎮兵擊之於定海北洋，衝賊為二，自當牽，急擊，逐至盡山。

translations.literal: In autumn Qian and Fen together invaded Zhejiang; Changgeng united the forces of the various garrisons and attacked them in the northern sea off Dinghai, splitting the bandits in two; he himself faced Qian, pressed the attack hotly, and pursued him to Jingshan.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn Qian and Fen invaded Zhejiang together. Changgeng united the garrison fleets and struck them in the northern sea off Dinghai, splitting the enemy force in two. He took Qian on himself, pressed the attack hard, and drove him as far as Jingshan.

sentences.zh: 牽以大艇得遁，委敗硃濆，濆怒，於是復分。

translations.literal: Qian escaped in his large junk and abandoned Zhu Fen to defeat; Fen was enraged, and they then split apart again.
translations.idiomatic: Qian escaped in his large junk and left Zhu Fen to be defeated; Fen was furious, and the two allies parted ways once more.

sentences.zh: 十年夏，調福建提督。

translations.literal: In the summer of the tenth year he was transferred to be naval commander-in-chief of Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of 1805 he was transferred to naval commander-in-chief of Fujian.

sentences.zh: 牽聞長庚至，遂竄浙，追敗之青龍港，又敗之於台州斗米洋。

translations.literal: When Qian heard that Changgeng had arrived, he fled into Zhejiang; Changgeng pursued and defeated him at Qinglong Port and again at Doumiyang off Taizhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Qian learned that Changgeng had arrived, he fled into Zhejiang, where Changgeng pursued and defeated him at Qinglong Port and again at Doumiyang off Taizhou.

sentences.zh: 復調浙江提督。

translations.literal: He was again transferred to be naval commander-in-chief of Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred back to naval commander-in-chief of Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 十一年正月，牽合百餘艘犯台灣，結土匪萬餘攻府城，自號鎮海王，沉舟鹿耳門阻援兵。

translations.literal: In the first month of the eleventh year Qian united more than a hundred vessels to invade Taiwan, joined with more than ten thousand local bandits to attack the prefectural city, styled himself King Who Pacifies the Sea, and sank ships at Luer Gate to block relief troops.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of 1806 Qian assembled more than a hundred vessels to invade Taiwan, allied with more than ten thousand local bandits to assault the prefectural seat, styled himself King Who Pacifies the Sea, and sank ships at Luer Gate to block relief forces.

sentences.zh: 長庚至，不得入，諜知南汕、北汕、大港門可通小舟，遣總兵許松年、副將王得祿繞道入，攻洲仔尾，連敗之。

translations.literal: When Changgeng arrived he could not enter; spies learned that South Shoal, North Shoal, and Dagang Gate could admit small boats; he sent Regional Commander Xu Songnian and Deputy Commander Wang Delu in by a detour to attack Zhouzaiwei and repeatedly defeated the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Changgeng arrived but could not force an entrance until scouts reported that South Shoal, North Shoal, and Dagang Gate could admit small boats. He sent Regional Commander Xu Songnian and Deputy Commander Wang Delu in by a roundabout route to attack Zhouzaiwei and defeated the enemy repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 二月，松年登洲仔尾，焚其藔，牽反救，長庚遣兵出南汕，與松年夾擊，大敗之。

translations.literal: In the second month Songnian landed at Zhouzaiwei and burned their stockades; Qian turned back to rescue them; Changgeng sent troops out from South Shoal to strike Qian in concert with Songnian and inflicted a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month Songnian landed at Zhouzaiwei and burned the pirate stockades. When Qian turned back to relieve them, Changgeng sent troops out from South Shoal to strike him in concert with Songnian and won a crushing victory.

sentences.zh: 牽無去路，困守北汕。

translations.literal: Qian had no way out and was trapped holding North Shoal.
translations.idiomatic: With no escape route left, Qian was trapped at North Shoal.

sentences.zh: 會風潮驟漲，沉舟漂起，乃奪鹿耳門逸去，詔奪花翎、頂戴。

translations.literal: Just then wind and tide rose sharply, the sunken ships floated up, and he seized Luer Gate and fled; an edict stripped Changgeng of his peacock feather and official cap insignia.
translations.idiomatic: Then wind and tide surged, the sunken blockships floated free, and Qian broke through Luer Gate and escaped. An edict stripped Changgeng of his peacock feather and cap insignia.

sentences.zh: 四月，蔡牽、硃濆同犯福寧外洋，擊敗之，追至台州斗米洋，擒其黨李按等。

translations.literal: In the fourth month Cai Qian and Zhu Fen together invaded the outer seas of Funing; he defeated them, pursued to Doumiyang off Taizhou, and captured their follower Li An and others.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month Cai Qian and Zhu Fen together raided the outer seas off Funing. Changgeng defeated them, pursued them to Doumiyang off Taizhou, and captured their follower Li An and others.

sentences.zh: 長庚疏言：「蔡逆未能殲擒者，實由兵船不得力，接濟未斷絕所致。

translations.literal: Changgeng memorialized: "The reason the rebel Cai has not yet been destroyed and captured is truly that the military ships are inadequate and supplies from shore have not been cut off."
translations.idiomatic: Changgeng memorialized: "The rebel Cai has not yet been destroyed and captured chiefly because our warships are inadequate and shore supply lines to the pirates have not been severed."

sentences.zh: 臣所乘之船，較各鎮為最大，及逼近牽船，尚低五六尺。

translations.literal: "The ship Your Servant rides is the largest among the various garrisons, yet when we close on Qian's vessel it is still five or six feet lower."
translations.idiomatic: "The vessel I command is the largest in the fleet, yet when we close with Qian's ship we still stand five or six feet lower."

sentences.zh: 曾與三鎮總兵原預支養廉，捐造大船十五號，而督臣以造船需數月之久，借帑四五萬之多，不肯具奏。

translations.literal: "I once advanced my official stipend together with the regional commanders of the three garrisons and donated funds to build fifteen large ships, but the governor argued that shipbuilding would take many months and borrowing forty or fifty thousand taels was too much, and refused to memorialize it."
translations.idiomatic: "I once pledged my official stipend together with the three garrison commanders to fund fifteen large ships, but the governor refused to memorialize the project, citing the months required to build them and a treasury loan of forty or fifty thousand taels."

sentences.zh: 且海賊無兩年不修之船，亦無一年不壞之槓料。

translations.literal: "Moreover, sea bandits have no ships that go two years without repair, nor spars and timbers that last a year without breaking."
translations.idiomatic: "Moreover, sea pirates do not keep ships that go two years without repair, nor spars and timbers that last a year without replacement."

sentences.zh: 桅柁折則船為虛器，風篷爛則寸步難行。

translations.literal: "If mast and rudder break, the ship becomes an empty shell; if sails rot, it can hardly move an inch."
translations.idiomatic: "Break the mast or rudder and the ship becomes useless; let the sails rot and it can barely move."

sentences.zh: 乃逆賊在鹿耳門竄出，僅餘船三十，篷朽硝缺；

translations.literal: "Yet when the rebel slipped out at Luer Gate he had only thirty ships left, with rotten sails and missing saltpeter;"
translations.idiomatic: "Yet when the rebel slipped out of Luer Gate he had only thirty ships left, with rotten sails and depleted powder stores;"

sentences.zh: 一回閩地，裝篷燂洗，煥然一新，糧藥充足，賊何日可滅？

translations.literal: "once back in Fujian territory he rigged sails, caulked and washed the hulls, and they were made wholly new, with ample grain and munitions—on what day can the bandits be extinguished?"
translations.idiomatic: "once he was back in Fujian he rerigged sails, recaulked and refitted the hulls until they looked new, and restocked grain and munitions in full—on what day can such bandits ever be destroyed?"

sentences.zh: 」詔逮治玉德，以阿林保代。

translations.literal: " An edict ordered Yu De arrested and punished, and Alinbao replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: " An edict ordered Yu De arrested and replaced him with Alinbao.

sentences.zh: 既至福建，諸文武吏以未協剿、未斷岸姦接濟、懼得罪​​，交譖長庚。

translations.literal: After he arrived in Fujian, civil and military officials, fearing punishment for failing to coordinate the campaign, failing to cut off coastal traitors' supplies, and offending authority, slandered Changgeng in concert.
translations.idiomatic: Once he reached Fujian, civil and military officials who feared punishment for poor coordination, failure to sever coastal supply lines to the pirates, and official censure joined in slandering Changgeng.

sentences.zh: 阿林保密劾其逗留，章三上，詔密詢浙江巡撫清安泰。

translations.literal: Alinbao secretly impeached him for lingering; three memorials were sent up; an edict secretly inquired of Zhejiang Grand Coordinator Qing Antai.
translations.idiomatic: Alinbao secretly impeached him for stalling, sent up three memorials, and the throne secretly asked Zhejiang Grand Coordinator Qing Antai for his view.

sentences.zh: 清安泰疏言：「長庚熟海島形勢、風雲沙線，每戰自持柁，老於操舟者不及。

translations.literal: Qing Antai memorialized: "Changgeng knows the shapes of the sea islands, the patterns of wind, cloud, and sandbars; in every battle he holds the helm himself, and veterans of steering cannot match him."
translations.idiomatic: Qing Antai replied: "Changgeng knows every island, wind pattern, and sandbar; in every battle he takes the helm himself, and veterans of the sea cannot match him."

sentences.zh: 兩年在軍，過門不入。

translations.literal: "For two years in the army he passed his own door without entering."
translations.idiomatic: "For two years on campaign he passed his own door without stopping."

sentences.zh: 以捐造船械，傾其家貲。

translations.literal: "To donate funds for ships and weapons he exhausted his family wealth."
translations.idiomatic: "He spent his family fortune donating ships and weapons to the fleet."

sentences.zh: 所俘獲盡以賞功，士爭效死。

translations.literal: "Everything captured he gave entirely as rewards for merit, and the troops vied to die for the cause."
translations.idiomatic: "He gave every capture entirely as reward for merit, and his men vied to fight to the death."

sentences.zh: 八月中戰漁山，圍攻蔡逆，火器瓦石雨下，身受多創，將士傷百四十人，鏖戰不退。

translations.literal: "In the eighth month he fought at Yushan, besieging the rebel Cai; firearms and stones rained down; he himself received many wounds, one hundred forty officers and soldiers were injured, yet he battled fiercely without retreating."
translations.idiomatic: "In the eighth month he fought at Yushan and besieged the rebel Cai while firearms and stones rained down. He took many wounds himself, one hundred forty officers and men were injured, yet he fought on without retreating."

sentences.zh: 賊中語：'不畏千萬兵，只畏李長庚。

translations.literal: "Among the bandits they say: 'We do not fear millions of troops, we fear only Li Changgeng.'"
translations.idiomatic: "Among the pirates they say: 'We do not fear millions of troops; we fear only Li Changgeng.'"

sentences.zh: '實水師諸將之冠。

translations.literal: "' He is truly the crown of the naval commanders."
translations.idiomatic: "' He is truly the foremost of the navy's commanders."

sentences.zh: 」且備陳海戰之難，非兩省合力不能成功狀。

translations.literal: " He also set forth in detail the difficulty of naval warfare and that success was impossible unless the two provinces united their strength."
translations.idiomatic: " He also explained in detail how hard naval warfare was and that the two provinces would have to combine their strength to succeed."

sentences.zh: 時同戰諸鎮，亦交章言長庚實非逗留。

translations.literal: At that time the various garrisons fighting alongside him also sent memorials one after another stating that Changgeng was truly not lingering.
translations.idiomatic: The garrison commanders fighting alongside him also sent memorial after memorial stating that Changgeng was not stalling.

sentences.zh: 仁宗震怒，切責阿林保，謂：「朕若輕信其言，豈不自失良將？

translations.literal: Emperor Renzong was greatly angered and sharply rebuked Alinbao, saying: "If I lightly believed his words, would I not have lost a fine general myself?"
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Renzong was furious and sharply rebuked Alinbao: "Had I believed him lightly, would I not have lost a fine general of my own?"

sentences.zh: 嗣後勦賊專倚長庚，儻阿林保從中掣肘，玉德即前車之鑑！

translations.literal: "Henceforth in suppressing bandits rely solely on Changgeng; if Alinbao obstructs from within, Yu De is the warning from the cart ahead!"
translations.idiomatic: "From now on rely on Changgeng alone to suppress the pirates. If Alinbao obstructs him from within, Yu De is the warning you should heed!"

sentences.zh: 」並飭造大同安梭船三十，未成以前，先僱商船備剿。

translations.literal: " He also ordered thirty large Tong'an-style patrol sloops built, and before they were finished, first hired merchant ships to prepare for the campaign."
translations.idiomatic: " He also ordered thirty large Tong'an-style patrol sloops built and, until they were ready, merchant vessels hired for the campaign."

sentences.zh: 長庚聞之，益感奮。

translations.literal: When Changgeng heard this he was all the more moved and inspired.
translations.idiomatic: When Changgeng heard this, his resolve burned all the brighter.

sentences.zh: 是年秋，擊賊於漁山，受傷，事聞，復還翎頂。

translations.literal: That autumn he attacked bandits at Yushan and was wounded; when the matter was reported, his feather and cap insignia were restored.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn he fought pirates at Yushan and was wounded; when the report reached court, his feather insignia and cap rank were restored.

sentences.zh: 十二年春，擊敗牽於粵洋大星嶼。

translations.literal: In the spring of the twelfth year he defeated Qian at Daxing Island in the Guangdong seas.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of 1807 he defeated Qian at Daxing Island in Guangdong waters.

sentences.zh: 十一月，又擊敗於閩洋浮鷹山。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month he defeated him again at Fuying Mountain in the Fujian seas.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month he defeated him again off Fuying Mountain in Fujian waters.

sentences.zh: 十二月，遂偕福建提督張見升追牽入澳，窮其所向，至黑水洋。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month he then joined Fujian Naval Commander-in-Chief Zhang Jiansheng in pursuing Qian into the outer seas, following him to the end of his course as far as the Black Water Sea.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month he joined Fujian Naval Commander-in-Chief Zhang Jiansheng in pursuing Qian into the open ocean, tracking him all the way to the Black Water Sea.

sentences.zh: 牽僅存三艇，皆百戰之寇，以死拒。

translations.literal: Qian had only three junks left, all veteran bandits who resisted to the death.
translations.idiomatic: Qian had only three junks left, crewed by hardened veterans who fought to the death.

sentences.zh: 長庚自以火攻船掛其艇尾，欲躍登，忽砲中喉，移時而殞。

translations.literal: Changgeng himself took a fire-attack ship and hooked it to the stern of Qian's junk, intending to leap aboard; suddenly a cannonball struck his throat, and after a time he died.
translations.idiomatic: Changgeng himself took a fire ship, hooked it to the stern of Qian's junk, and was about to board when a cannonball struck his throat; he died shortly afterward.

sentences.zh: 時戰艦數十倍於賊，見升庸懦，遙見總統船亂，遽退，牽乃遁入安南外洋。

translations.literal: At the time the warships were many times more numerous than the bandits; Jiansheng was mediocre and cowardly; from afar he saw the commander-in-chief's ship in disorder and hastily withdrew, and Qian then fled into the outer seas beyond Annam.
translations.idiomatic: The fleet outnumbered the pirates many times over, but Jiansheng was timid and incompetent. Seeing the commander's ship in disorder from a distance, he withdrew at once, and Qian escaped into the open sea beyond Annam.

sentences.zh: 上震悼，褒血卩，初擬俟寇平錫以伯爵，乃追封三等壯烈伯，諡忠毅，於原籍建專祠。

translations.literal: The emperor was deeply shaken and mourned him, bestowing posthumous honors; it had first been planned to grant him a marquisate once the bandits were pacified, but he was posthumously enfeoffed as Baron of Fierce Valor, third rank, with the posthumous title Loyal and Resolute, and a dedicated shrine was built in his native place.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was deeply grieved and lavished posthumous honors on him. He had been slated for a marquisate once the pirates were destroyed, but was instead posthumously enfeoffed as Baron of Fierce Valor, third rank, with the posthumous title Loyal and Resolute, and a dedicated shrine was built in his home district.

sentences.zh: 長庚治軍嚴，信賞必罰，自偏裨下至隊長水手，耳目心志如一，人人皆可用。

translations.literal: Changgeng governed the army strictly, rewarding faithfully and punishing surely; from deputy commanders down to squad leaders and sailors, ears, eyes, mind, and will were as one, and every man could be used.
translations.idiomatic: Changgeng ran a strict command with faithful rewards and certain punishments. From his deputies down to squad leaders and ordinary sailors, every man moved as one will, and each was fit for use.

sentences.zh: 與阮元同心整厲水師，數建功，為玉德所忌。

translations.literal: He worked in one mind with Ruan Yuan to reorganize and strengthen the navy, achieved merit many times, and was envied by Yu De.
translations.idiomatic: Working in concert with Ruan Yuan, he reorganized and strengthened the navy and won repeated victories, which drew Yu De's resentment.

sentences.zh: 及阿林保之至閩也，置酒款長庚，謂曰：「大海捕魚，何時入網？

translations.literal: When Alinbao arrived in Fujian he set out wine to entertain Changgeng and said: "Fishing in the great sea—when will the fish enter the net?"
translations.idiomatic: When Alinbao reached Fujian he entertained Changgeng with wine and said, "Fishing the open sea—when will the catch ever land in the net?"

sentences.zh: 海外事無左證，公但斬一酋，以牽首報，我飛章告捷，以餘賊歸善後辦理。

translations.literal: "Matters beyond the sea have no corroborating witnesses; you need only behead one chieftain and report it as Qian's head; I will fly a memorial announcing victory, and leave the remaining bandits for later settlement."
translations.idiomatic: "Out at sea there are no witnesses. You need only cut off one chieftain's head and report it as Qian's. I will rush a victory memorial to court and leave the rest for later cleanup."

sentences.zh: 公受上賞，我亦邀次功，孰與窮年冒風濤僥倖萬一哉？

translations.literal: "You will receive the highest reward, and I too will claim a secondary merit—is that not better than spending years braving wind and waves for a one-in-ten-thousand chance?"
translations.idiomatic: "You take the highest reward and I claim a share of the credit. Is that not better than spending years in wind and waves for a one-in-ten-thousand chance?"

sentences.zh: 」長庚謝曰：「吾何能為此？

translations.literal: " Changgeng declined and said: "How could I do such a thing?"
translations.idiomatic: " Changgeng declined. "How could I do such a thing?"

sentences.zh: 久視海船如廬舍，誓與賊同死，不與同生！

translations.literal: "For long I have regarded sea ships as my lodge; I swear to die with the bandits and not to live with them!"
translations.idiomatic: "I have long treated my ship as home. I swear to die with the pirates rather than live while they do!"

sentences.zh: 」阿林保不懌。

translations.literal: " Alinbao was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: " Alinbao was displeased.

sentences.zh: 既屢劾不得逞，則飛檄趣戰。

translations.literal: Since repeated impeachments did not succeed, he then sent urgent dispatches pressing for battle.
translations.idiomatic: When repeated impeachments failed, he sent urgent dispatches pressing for battle.

sentences.zh: 長庚緘所落齒寄其妻，志以身殉國。

translations.literal: Changgeng sealed the teeth he had lost and sent them to his wife, resolved to die for the state.
translations.idiomatic: Changgeng sealed the teeth he had lost and sent them to his wife, resolved to die for the state.

sentences.zh: 既歿，詔部將王得祿、邱良功嗣任，勉以同心敵愾​​，為長庚雪仇。

translations.literal: After his death an edict ordered his subordinate commanders Wang Delu and Qiu Lianggong to succeed him, urging them to unite in hatred of the enemy and avenge Changgeng.
translations.idiomatic: After his death an edict appointed his subordinates Wang Delu and Qiu Lianggong to succeed him, urging them to unite against the enemy and avenge Changgeng.

sentences.zh: 二人遵其部勒，卒滅蔡牽，竟全功焉。

translations.literal: The two men followed his regulations and in the end destroyed Cai Qian, fully completing the achievement.
translations.idiomatic: The two men followed his regulations, destroyed Cai Qian in the end, and brought the campaign to full completion.

sentences.zh: 長庚無子，養同姓子廷鈺為嗣，襲伯爵，授二等侍衛。

translations.literal: Changgeng had no son; he adopted a clansman named Ting Yu as heir, who inherited the barony and was appointed a second-rank imperial bodyguard.
translations.idiomatic: Changgeng had no son and adopted a clansman, Ting Yu, as his heir. Ting Yu inherited the barony and was appointed a second-rank imperial bodyguard.

sentences.zh: 道光中，出為南昌副將，累擢浙江提督。

translations.literal: In the Daoguang reign he went out to serve as deputy commander at Nanchang and was repeatedly promoted to naval commander-in-chief of Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Under Daoguang he was posted as deputy commander at Nanchang and rose through successive promotions to naval commander-in-chief of Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 因病不能巡洋，奪職家居。

translations.literal: Because of illness he could not patrol the seas, was stripped of office, and lived at home.
translations.idiomatic: Illness kept him from patrolling the coast, and he was dismissed to live at home.

sentences.zh: 咸豐初，治本籍團練，迭克廈門、金島、仙遊，授福建提督。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Xianfeng reign he organized local militia in his native place, repeatedly captured Xiamen, Jindao, and Xianyou, and was appointed naval commander-in-chief of Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Xianfeng reign he organized local militia in his home district, recaptured Xiamen, Jindao, and Xianyou in succession, and was appointed naval commander-in-chief of Fujian.

sentences.zh: 尋以誤報軍情解任，仍會辦團練。

translations.literal: Soon he was removed from office for falsely reporting military intelligence, but continued to assist in organizing the militia.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon removed for misreporting military intelligence but continued to assist with militia organization.

sentences.zh: 十一年，卒，孫經寶襲爵。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he died, and his grandson Jingbao inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: In 1861 he died, and his grandson Jingbao inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 胡振聲，亦同安人，提督貴子。

translations.literal: Hu Zhensheng was also a native of Tong'an and the son of Naval Commander-in-Chief Hu Gui.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Zhensheng, also from Tong'an, was the son of Naval Commander-in-Chief Hu Gui.

sentences.zh: 起行伍，累擢至溫州鎮總兵。

translations.literal: He rose from the ranks and was repeatedly promoted to regional commander of the Wenzhou Garrison.
translations.idiomatic: He rose from the ranks and was promoted in succession to regional commander of the Wenzhou Garrison.

sentences.zh: 從長庚大破夷艇於台州松門洋，自是屢從長庚擊賊海上。

translations.literal: Following Changgeng he helped inflict a great defeat on foreign junks at Songmen off Taizhou, and from then on repeatedly followed Changgeng in attacking bandits at sea.
translations.idiomatic: Serving under Changgeng, he helped win a major victory over foreign junks at Songmen off Taizhou and thereafter fought beside him at sea again and again.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶九年六月，率二十六艘運舟材赴福建，至浮鷹洋，遇賊，與總兵孫大剛夾攻，殲賊甚眾，而舟為砲焚，閩師不能救，遂被害。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the ninth year of Jiaqing he led twenty-six vessels transporting ship timber to Fujian; at the Fuying seas they met bandits; together with Regional Commander Sun Dagang they attacked from both sides and destroyed many bandits, but his ship was burned by cannon fire, the Fujian fleet could not rescue him, and he was killed.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of 1804 he led twenty-six vessels carrying ship timber to Fujian. Off Fuying they met pirates and, with Regional Commander Sun Dagang, attacked from both sides and destroyed a large enemy force. His ship was burned by cannon fire, the Fujian fleet could not reach him in time, and he was killed.

sentences.zh: 優恤，諡武壯，予騎都尉兼雲騎尉世職。

translations.literal: He received generous condolence rewards, was given the posthumous title Martial and Robust, and was granted the hereditary offices of Cavalry Commandant and Cloud Cavalry Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: He received generous posthumous honors, was given the posthumous title Martial and Robust, and was granted the hereditary offices of Cavalry Commandant and Cloud Cavalry Commandant.

sentences.zh: 王得祿，字玉峰，福建嘉義人。

translations.literal: Wang Delu, courtesy name Yufeng, was a native of Jiayi in Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Delu, whose courtesy name was Yufeng, came from Jiayi in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 林爽文倡亂，陷縣城。

translations.literal: When Lin Shuangwen raised rebellion, the county seat fell.
translations.idiomatic: When Lin Shuangwen raised his rebellion, the county seat fell.

sentences.zh: 得祿家素豐，捐貲募鄉勇，助官軍復之，授把總。

translations.literal: Delu's family had long been wealthy; he donated funds to recruit local militia, helped the government army recover the city, and was appointed a platoon leader.
translations.idiomatic: Delu came from a wealthy family. He donated funds to raise local militia, helped government troops recover the city, and was appointed a platoon leader.

sentences.zh: 明年，賊复圍城，從總兵柴大紀固守。

translations.literal: The next year the bandits again besieged the city; he followed Regional Commander Chai Daji in holding it fast.
translations.idiomatic: The next year the rebels besieged the city again, and he followed Regional Commander Chai Daji in holding the defenses.

sentences.zh: 及圍解，率鄉勇搜捕大坪頂等處餘匪，焚瑯嶠賊巢，賊渠莊大田就擒。

translations.literal: When the siege was lifted he led local militia to search out and capture remaining bandits at Dapingding and other places, burned the bandit lair at Langjiao, and the bandit leader Zhuang Datian was taken.
translations.idiomatic: After the siege was lifted he led local militia to hunt down remaining rebels around Dapingding, burned the rebel stronghold at Langjiao, and captured the rebel leader Zhuang Datian.

sentences.zh: 台灣平，賜花翎、五品頂戴，遷千總。

translations.literal: When Taiwan was pacified he was granted the peacock feather and fifth-rank cap insignia and was promoted to company commander.
translations.idiomatic: When Taiwan was pacified he was awarded the peacock feather and fifth-rank cap insignia and promoted to company commander.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶元年，巡洋至獺窟，遇賊，得祿先登，擒吳興信等。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jiaqing, while patrolling the coast he reached Taxue; he met bandits, Delu was first to board, and captured Wu Xingxin and others.
translations.idiomatic: In 1796, while on coastal patrol, he reached Taxue, encountered pirates, boarded first, and captured Wu Xingxin and others.

sentences.zh: 歷年出洋捕海盜，號勇敢，累擢金門營游擊。

translations.literal: Year after year he went to sea to capture pirates, was known as brave, and was repeatedly promoted to battalion officer of the Jinmen Garrison.
translations.idiomatic: Year after year he patrolled the coast against pirates, earned a reputation for courage, and rose in succession to battalion officer of the Jinmen Garrison.

sentences.zh: 七年，從李長庚擊蔡牽於東滬洋，擒賊目徐業等百餘人，又擒呂送於崇武洋，被獎敘。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he followed Li Changgeng in attacking Cai Qian at Donghu seas, captured more than a hundred bandit chiefs including Xu Ye, and also captured Lü Song at Chongwu seas, and received commendation.
translations.idiomatic: In 1802 he fought under Li Changgeng against Cai Qian at Donghu, captured more than a hundred pirate leaders including Xu Ye, and also took Lü Song off Chongwu, earning official commendation.

sentences.zh: 九年，從總兵羅仁太擊賊於虎頭山洋面，獲船械甚多。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he followed Regional Commander Luo Rentai in attacking bandits on the seas off Hutou Mountain and seized many ships and weapons.
translations.idiomatic: In 1804 he fought under Regional Commander Luo Rentai against pirates off Hutou Mountain and seized a large quantity of ships and arms.

sentences.zh: 十年，擊蔡牽於虎井洋，敗之，署澎湖協副將。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he attacked Cai Qian at Hujing seas, defeated him, and acted as deputy commander of the Penghu Garrison.
translations.idiomatic: In 1805 he defeated Cai Qian at Hujing and served in an acting capacity as deputy commander of the Penghu Garrison.

sentences.zh: 九月，遇牽於水澳，焚其舟，擒殲硃列等百餘人。

translations.literal: In the ninth month he met Qian at Shuiao, burned his ships, and captured and destroyed more than a hundred men including Zhu Lie.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he met Qian at Shuiao, burned his vessels, and killed or captured more than a hundred men including Zhu Lie.

sentences.zh: 十一年春，牽入台灣，圍府城。

translations.literal: In the spring of the eleventh year Qian entered Taiwan and besieged the prefectural city.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of 1806 Qian invaded Taiwan and besieged the prefectural seat.

sentences.zh: 李長庚令得祿與許松年駕小舟自安平港入偵之，帆檣彌望，夜縱火焚賊舟，遂入屯柴頭港。

translations.literal: Li Changgeng ordered Delu and Xu Songnian to take small boats in from Anping Harbor to reconnoiter; sails and masts filled the view; at night they set fires and burned the bandit ships, then entered and encamped at Chaitou Harbor.
translations.idiomatic: Li Changgeng sent Delu and Xu Songnian in small boats from Anping Harbor to scout the enemy. Sails filled the horizon; that night they set fire to the pirate fleet, then landed and encamped at Chaitou Harbor.

sentences.zh: 明日，賊自洲仔尾攻府城北門，得祿率兵躡其後，大呼以前，賊驚卻。

translations.literal: The next day the bandits from Zhouzaiwei attacked the north gate of the prefectural city; Delu led troops to follow on their heels, shouting as he advanced, and the bandits fell back in alarm.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the pirates attacked the north gate from Zhouzaiwei. Delu led troops up behind them, shouting as he charged, and the enemy fell back in alarm.

sentences.zh: 城內軍出夾攻，大敗之，乘勝至洲仔尾，破其營，賊乃遁。

translations.literal: The troops inside the city came out to attack from both sides and inflicted a great defeat; pressing the advantage they reached Zhouzaiwei, broke the camp, and the bandits then fled.
translations.idiomatic: Troops from inside the city sallied out to attack from both sides and won a crushing victory. Pressing the advantage, they reached Zhouzaiwei, destroyed the camp, and the pirates fled.

sentences.zh: 五月，牽复竄鹿耳門，得祿首先沖擊，獲船十，沈船十一。

translations.literal: In the fifth month Qian again slipped into Luer Gate; Delu was first to charge, captured ten ships, and sank eleven.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Qian slipped back toward Luer Gate. Delu led the charge, captured ten ships, and sank eleven.

sentences.zh: 敘功，加總兵銜。

translations.literal: His merit was recorded and he was given the brevet rank of regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: His merits were recorded and he was given the brevet rank of regional commander.

sentences.zh: 尋擢福寧鎮總兵。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to regional commander of the Funing Garrison.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to regional commander of the Funing Garrison.

sentences.zh: 十二年，調南澳鎮。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he was transferred to the Nan'ao Garrison.
translations.idiomatic: In 1807 he was transferred to the Nan'ao Garrison.

sentences.zh: 七月，敗硃濆於雞籠洋，獲船十四。

translations.literal: In the seventh month he defeated Zhu Fen at Jilong seas and captured fourteen ships.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month he defeated Zhu Fen off Jilong and captured fourteen ships.

sentences.zh: 十一月，又敗其黨於古雷洋，射殪賊目硃金，擒張祈，被獎敘。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month he again defeated their faction at Gulei seas, shot and killed the bandit chief Zhu Jin, captured Zhang Qi, and received commendation.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month he defeated their allies again off Gulei, shot dead the pirate chief Zhu Jin, captured Zhang Qi, and earned commendation.

sentences.zh: 未幾，李長庚戰歿，命得祿與邱良功繼任軍事。

translations.literal: Before long Li Changgeng died in battle; Delu and Qiu Lianggong were ordered to succeed to military command.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Li Changgeng fell in battle, and Delu and Qiu Lianggong were ordered to take over command.

sentences.zh: 十三年，擢浙江提督。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he was promoted to naval commander-in-chief of Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: In 1808 he was promoted to naval commander-in-chief of Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 既而調福建，邱良功代之。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Fujian, and Qiu Lianggong replaced him in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to Fujian, with Qiu Lianggong taking his place in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 時阮元再任浙江巡撫，張師誠為福建巡撫，兩省合力，得祿與良功同心滅賊。

translations.literal: At that time Ruan Yuan again served as grand coordinator of Zhejiang and Zhang Shicheng as grand coordinator of Fujian; the two provinces united their strength, and Delu and Lianggong worked in one mind to destroy the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Ruan Yuan was again grand coordinator of Zhejiang and Zhang Shicheng grand coordinator of Fujian. With the two provinces cooperating, Delu and Lianggong worked as one to destroy the pirates.

sentences.zh: 十四年八月，同擊蔡牽於定海漁山，敗之。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the fourteenth year they jointly attacked Cai Qian at Yushan off Dinghai and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of 1809 they jointly attacked Cai Qian at Yushan off Dinghai and defeated him.

sentences.zh: 牽東南走，追至黑水洋，合擊累日，良功以浙舟駢列賊舟東，得祿率閩舟列浙舟東，戰酣，良功舟傷暫退，得祿舟進，附牽舟，諸賊黨隔不得援。

translations.literal: Qian fled southeast; they pursued to the Black Water Sea and fought together for many days; Lianggong lined Zhejiang ships abreast to the east of Qian's junk, Delu led Fujian ships east of the Zhejiang line; as the battle grew fierce Lianggong's ship was damaged and withdrew briefly, Delu's ship advanced and grappled Qian's junk, and the bandit followers were cut off and could not reinforce.
translations.idiomatic: Qian fled southeast to the Black Water Sea, where the allies fought him for days. Lianggong lined the Zhejiang ships along the enemy's east side while Delu placed the Fujian fleet east of them. In the heat of battle Lianggong's ship was damaged and fell back briefly; Delu pressed forward, grappled Qian's junk, and cut off the pirate followers from reinforcing.

sentences.zh: 牽鉛丸盡，以番銀代，得祿額腕皆傷，擲火焚牽舟尾樓，复衝斷其柁。

translations.literal: Qian's lead shot was exhausted and he used foreign silver in its place; Delu's forehead and wrists were all wounded; he threw fire and burned the stern tower of Qian's junk, then charged again and broke off its rudder.
translations.idiomatic: Qian ran out of lead shot and used foreign silver coins instead. Delu was wounded in the forehead and both wrists, hurled fire that burned the stern tower of Qian's junk, then charged again and broke off its rudder.

sentences.zh: 牽知不免，舉砲自裂其舟沉於海。

translations.literal: Qian knew he could not escape, raised a cannon, and blew his own ship apart so that it sank into the sea.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing no escape, Qian fired his own cannon into the hull and sank his ship.

sentences.zh: 詔以牽肆逆十有四年，渠魁就殲，厥功甚偉，錫封得祿二等子爵，賜雙眼花翎。

translations.literal: An edict noted that Qian had rebelled for fourteen years and the ringleader was now destroyed, a very great achievement; Delu was enfeoffed as second-rank viscount and granted the double-eyed peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: An edict noted that Qian had ravaged the coast for fourteen years and that destroying the ringleader was a signal achievement. Delu was enfeoffed as second-rank viscount and granted the double-eyed peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 餘黨千二百人，後皆降，海盜遂息。

translations.literal: The remaining followers, twelve hundred men, later all surrendered, and piracy then ceased.
translations.idiomatic: The remaining twelve hundred followers later surrendered, and coastal piracy finally subsided.

sentences.zh: 得祿為福建提督歷十載，屢疏陳緝捕事宜，改定水師船制，皆如議行。

translations.literal: Delu served ten years as naval commander-in-chief of Fujian, repeatedly memorializing on matters of pursuit and capture, and revising the naval ship regulations, all of which were carried out as proposed.
translations.idiomatic: Delu spent ten years as Fujian naval commander-in-chief, repeatedly memorializing on coastal defense and revising naval ship regulations, all of which were adopted as he proposed.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，調浙江提督。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year he was transferred to naval commander-in-chief of Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: In 1820 he was transferred to naval commander-in-chief of Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 道光元年，乞病歸。

translations.literal: In the first year of Daoguang he begged leave on grounds of illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: In 1821 he retired on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 十二年，台灣張丙作亂，得祿率家屬擒賊目張紅頭等，加太子少保。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year Zhang Bing raised rebellion in Taiwan; Delu led his family members to capture the bandit chief Zhang Hongtou and others, and was made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In 1832 Zhang Bing rebelled in Taiwan. Delu led his family to capture the rebel chief Zhang Hongtou and others and was made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 十八年，台匪沈和肆掠，輸糧助守，晉太子太保。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year the Taiwan bandit Shen He plundered freely; Delu supplied grain to aid the defense and was promoted to Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In 1838 the Taiwan bandit Shen He raided widely. Delu supplied grain to aid the defense and was promoted to Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，英吉利犯廈門，命駐守澎湖。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year England attacked Xiamen; he was ordered to garrison Penghu.
translations.idiomatic: In 1841, when Britain attacked Xiamen, he was ordered to garrison Penghu.

sentences.zh: 次年，卒，贈伯爵，諡果毅。

translations.literal: The next year he died and was posthumously granted the rank of earl with the posthumous title Resolute and Bold.
translations.idiomatic: He died the following year and was posthumously granted the rank of earl with the posthumous title Resolute and Bold.

sentences.zh: 次子朝綸襲子爵，官戶部員外郎。

translations.literal: His second son Chaolun inherited the viscountcy and served as a secretary in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: His second son Chaolun inherited the viscountcy and served as a secretary in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 邱良功，福建同安人。

translations.literal: Qiu Lianggong was a native of Tong'an in Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu Lianggong came from Tong'an in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 起行伍，屢以獲盜功，洊擢閩安協副將。

translations.literal: He rose from the ranks, repeatedly won merit for capturing bandits, and was repeatedly promoted to deputy commander of the Min'an Garrison.
translations.idiomatic: He rose from the ranks, won repeated merit for capturing pirates, and was promoted in succession to deputy commander of the Min'an Garrison.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶十年，偕許松年會剿蔡牽，追至小琉球，見台灣師船二為賊圍，赴援，松年舉旗招之，未至。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Jiaqing he joined Xu Songnian in a joint campaign against Cai Qian and pursued to Little Ryukyu; he saw two Taiwan government ships surrounded by bandits and went to rescue them; Songnian raised flags to summon him, but he did not arrive.
translations.idiomatic: In 1805 he joined Xu Songnian in a joint campaign against Cai Qian and pursued as far as Little Ryukyu. Seeing two Taiwan government ships surrounded by pirates, he went to their aid, but Songnian's signals summoning him went unanswered.

sentences.zh: 以違調遣被劾，褫職逮訊。

translations.literal: He was impeached for disobeying orders, stripped of office, and arrested for interrogation.
translations.idiomatic: He was impeached for disobeying orders, stripped of office, and arrested for investigation.

sentences.zh: 得白，復原官，署台灣副將。

translations.literal: He was cleared, restored to his former office, and acted as deputy commander of Taiwan.
translations.idiomatic: He was cleared, restored to his former rank, and served in an acting capacity as deputy commander of Taiwan.

sentences.zh: 十一年春，從李長庚擊蔡牽，破洲仔尾賊巢，牽乘間逸，奪頂戴。

translations.literal: In the spring of the eleventh year he followed Li Changgeng in attacking Cai Qian, broke the bandit nest at Zhouzaiwei, but Qian slipped away in the interval and Lianggong's cap insignia was stripped.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of 1806 he fought under Li Changgeng against Cai Qian and destroyed the nest at Zhouzaiwei, but Qian slipped away and Lianggong was stripped of his cap insignia.

sentences.zh: 五月，破牽於鹿耳門，賜花翎。

translations.literal: In the fifth month he defeated Qian at Luer Gate and was granted the peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month he defeated Qian at Luer Gate and was awarded the peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 十二年，硃濆犯淡水，偕王得祿追至雞籠洋，連敗之，擒殲甚眾，被優敘。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year Zhu Fen invaded Tamsui; together with Wang Delu he pursued to Jilong seas, repeatedly defeated him, captured and destroyed a great many, and received superior commendation.
translations.idiomatic: In 1807 Zhu Fen raided Tamsui. Lianggong and Wang Delu pursued him to Jilong, defeated him repeatedly, killed or captured a great many, and received superior commendation.

sentences.zh: 十三年，擢浙江定海鎮總兵。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he was promoted to regional commander of the Dinghai Garrison in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: In 1808 he was promoted to regional commander of the Dinghai Garrison in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 十四年，擢浙江提督。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he was promoted to naval commander-in-chief of Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: In 1809 he was promoted to naval commander-in-chief of Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 偕王得祿合擊蔡牽於漁山外洋，乘上風逼之，夜半浪急，不得進。

translations.literal: Together with Wang Delu he jointly attacked Cai Qian in the outer seas off Yushan, used the wind advantage to press him, but at midnight the waves were fierce and they could not advance.
translations.idiomatic: With Wang Delu he attacked Cai Qian in the open sea off Yushan and used the wind to press him, but at midnight the seas were too rough to advance.

sentences.zh: 明日，复要截環攻，牽且戰且走，傍午逾黑水洋，見綠水。

translations.literal: The next day they again tried to intercept and surround him in attack; Qian fought while retreating; by noon they had passed the Black Water Sea and saw green water.
translations.idiomatic: The next day they tried again to intercept and encircle him. Qian fought as he fled, and by noon they had crossed the Black Water Sea into green water.

sentences.zh: 良功恐日暮賊遁，大呼突進，以己舟逼牽舟，兩篷相結。

translations.literal: Lianggong feared the bandits would escape at dusk; he shouted and charged forward, pressed his own junk against Qian's junk, and the two sails became entangled.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing the pirates would escape at dusk, Lianggong shouted and charged, driving his junk against Qian's until their sails locked together.

sentences.zh: 賊以椗衝船，陷入死鬥。

translations.literal: The bandits used grappling irons to ram the ship, and both sides were locked in a fight to the death.
translations.idiomatic: The pirates grappled the ships with iron hooks, and both sides were locked in a fight to the death.

sentences.zh: 良功腓被矛傷，毀賊椗，得脫出。

translations.literal: Lianggong's calf was wounded by a spear; he destroyed the bandits' grappling irons and was able to break free.
translations.idiomatic: Lianggong was wounded in the calf by a spear, smashed the enemy grappling hooks, and broke free.

sentences.zh: 閩師繼之，牽遂裂舟自沉。

translations.literal: The Fujian fleet followed up, and Qian then blew his ship apart and sank himself.
translations.idiomatic: The Fujian fleet pressed the attack, and Qian blew his ship apart and went down with it.

sentences.zh: 論功，錫封三等男爵，次於王得祿。

translations.literal: When merit was assessed he was enfeoffed as third-rank baron, ranking below Wang Delu.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit he was enfeoffed as third-rank baron, ranking below Wang Delu.

sentences.zh: 或為之不平，良功曰：「海疆肅清，已為快事，名位軒輊何足計？

translations.literal: Some were indignant on his behalf; Lianggong said: "The maritime frontier is now pacified—that is already a joy; why bother over the high or low of rank and title?"
translations.idiomatic: Some protested on his behalf, but Lianggong said, "The coast is pacified—that is joy enough. Why fret over differences in rank?"

sentences.zh: 」二十二年，入覲，卒於途，賜卹，諡剛勇。

translations.literal: " In the twenty-second year he went to court audience and died on the journey; condolence gifts were granted and he was given the posthumous title Bold and Brave.
translations.idiomatic: " In 1817 he set out for an audience at court and died on the journey. Condolence gifts were granted and he was given the posthumous title Bold and Brave.

sentences.zh: 子聯恩襲男爵，官直隸河間協副將。

translations.literal: His son Lian'en inherited the barony and served as deputy commander of the Hejian Garrison in Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: His son Lian'en inherited the barony and served as deputy commander of the Hejian Garrison in Zhili.

sentences.zh: 陳步雲，浙江瑞安人。

translations.literal: Chen Buyun was a native of Ruian in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Buyun came from Ruian in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 入伍隸水師，數獲盜，以勇力稱，授溫州營把總。

translations.literal: He entered the army and was attached to the navy; he captured bandits many times, was known for courage and strength, and was appointed a platoon leader in the Wenzhou Garrison.
translations.idiomatic: He enlisted in the navy, captured pirates repeatedly, earned a reputation for courage and strength, and was appointed a platoon leader in the Wenzhou Garrison.

sentences.zh: 從良功追蔡牽，步雲以四十人駕舟徑逼牽艦鏖鬥，舟小不相當，見兩提督至，亟投火罐焚賊艦，以長戟鉤舷，率數卒躍登，短兵相搏，殲牽妻及其黨。

translations.literal: Following Lianggong in pursuit of Cai Qian, Buyun took forty men in a boat and pressed straight against Qian's flagship in fierce combat; his boat was small and no match; when he saw the two commanders-in-chief arrive he quickly threw fire pots to burn the bandit ship, hooked the rail with a long halberd, led several soldiers in leaping aboard, fought hand to hand at close quarters, and destroyed Qian's wife and her followers.
translations.idiomatic: Pursuing Cai Qian under Lianggong, Buyun took forty men in a small boat and closed with Qian's flagship. When the two commanders-in-chief arrived, he hurled fire pots onto the pirate ship, hooked the rail with a long halberd, led several men aboard, fought hand to hand, and killed Qian's wife and her followers.

sentences.zh: 賊艦已壞，牽猶持利刃踞柁樓，顧欲取之。

translations.literal: The bandit ship was already ruined, yet Qian still grasped a sharp blade and crouched on the rudder tower, turning back as if to take Buyun.
translations.idiomatic: The pirate ship was already crippled, but Qian still held a blade on the rudder tower and turned as if to strike Buyun down.

sentences.zh: 良功隔船疾呼，船與水平，速去，放長繩水中援之起，而牽船沒矣。

translations.literal: Lianggong shouted urgently from the other ship: "The ship is level with the water—leave quickly!" He lowered a long rope into the water and hauled Buyun up, and Qian's ship sank.
translations.idiomatic: Lianggong shouted from the other ship, "Your boat is level with the water—get out now!" He lowered a rope into the sea and hauled Buyun up just as Qian's ship went under.

sentences.zh: 步雲身被十數創，兩提督皆臨慰視。

translations.literal: Buyun's body bore more than a dozen wounds; both commanders-in-chief came in person to comfort and inspect him.
translations.idiomatic: Buyun bore more than a dozen wounds, and both commanders-in-chief came in person to comfort him.

sentences.zh: 事聞，賜獎武銀牌，擢千總。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported he was granted a martial silver medal and promoted to company commander.
translations.idiomatic: When the report reached court he was awarded a martial silver medal and promoted to company commander.

sentences.zh: 累遷閩安副將。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to deputy commander of Min'an.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in succession to deputy commander of Min'an.

sentences.zh: 總督孫爾準欲裁減師船，步雲言李提督所造船高大堅緻，其利遠勝同安夾板、快駒諸船、裁之緝匪無具，有事不能制敵，議乃寢。

translations.literal: Governor-General Sun Erzhun wished to cut back naval ships; Buyun said the ships built by Commander Li were tall, large, solid, and fine, and their advantage far surpassed Tong'an double-planked ships, swift colts, and other vessels; to cut them would leave pursuit of bandits without tools, and in an emergency they could not master the enemy; the proposal was then dropped.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-General Sun Erzhun proposed cutting back naval ships. Buyun argued that the vessels built under Commander Li were large, solid, and far superior to Tong'an double-planked ships and swift colts; scrapping them would leave the navy without the means to hunt pirates or defeat the enemy in a crisis. The proposal was dropped.

sentences.zh: 爾準薦其才可勝專閫，入覲，宣宗曰：「汝即隨邱、王兩提督攻沉蔡牽之陳步雲耶？

translations.literal: Erzhun recommended that his talent could fill an independent command; on entering audience, Emperor Xuanzong said: "Are you Chen Buyun, who followed Commanders Qiu and Wang in sinking Cai Qian?"
translations.idiomatic: Erzhun recommended him for independent command. At court audience Emperor Xuanzong asked, "Are you Chen Buyun, who fought under Commanders Qiu and Wang to sink Cai Qian?"

sentences.zh: 」詢戰功甚悉。

translations.literal: " He inquired about his battle achievements in great detail.
translations.idiomatic: " He questioned him closely about the battle.

sentences.zh: 遂擢定海鎮總兵，歷瓊州、福寧、金門、海壇諸鎮。

translations.literal: He was then promoted to regional commander of the Dinghai Garrison and served in succession at the Qiongzhou, Funing, Jinmen, and Haitan garrisons.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to regional commander of the Dinghai Garrison and later held commands at Qiongzhou, Funing, Jinmen, and Haitan.

sentences.zh: 道光十九年，以傷發，乞解職。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year of Daoguang his old wounds reopened and he begged to be relieved of office.
translations.idiomatic: In 1839 his old wounds reopened and he requested retirement.

sentences.zh: 三十年，卒。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 1850.

sentences.zh: 許松年，字蓉俊，浙江瑞安人。

translations.literal: Xu Songnian, courtesy name Rongjun, was a native of Ruian in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Songnian, whose courtesy name was Rongjun, came from Ruian in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 以武舉效力水師，從李長庚積功至提標參將。

translations.literal: As a military licentiate he served in the navy, followed Li Changgeng, and through accumulated merit rose to brigade commander under the provincial commander.
translations.idiomatic: A military licentiate, he served in the navy under Li Changgeng and rose through accumulated merit to brigade commander on the provincial staff.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶十年，護理金門鎮總兵。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Jiaqing he acted as regional commander of the Jinmen Garrison.
translations.idiomatic: In 1805 he served in an acting capacity as regional commander of the Jinmen Garrison.

sentences.zh: 擊蔡牽於小琉球；

translations.literal: He attacked Cai Qian at Little Ryukyu;
translations.idiomatic: He fought Cai Qian at Little Ryukyu;

sentences.zh: 又擊硃濆、烏石二於宮仔洋，從李長庚追敗之於閩、粵交界甲子洋。

translations.literal: again attacked Zhu Fen and Wushi Er at Gongzai seas, and following Li Changgeng pursued and defeated them at Jiazi seas on the Fujian-Guangdong border.
translations.idiomatic: attacked Zhu Fen and Wushi Er at Gongzai, and under Li Changgeng pursued and defeated them at Jiazi on the Fujian-Guangdong border.

sentences.zh: 又迭擊牽於青龍港、斗米洋。

translations.literal: He again repeatedly attacked Qian at Qinglong Port and Doumiyang.
translations.idiomatic: He fought Qian repeatedly at Qinglong Port and Doumiyang.

sentences.zh: 十一年，偕王得祿敗牽於台灣洲仔尾，跐海水而登，焚溺無算。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, together with Wang Delu, he defeated Qian at Zhouzaiwei in Taiwan, waded through seawater to land, and burned and drowned countless enemies.
translations.idiomatic: In 1806 he and Wang Delu defeated Qian at Zhouzaiwei in Taiwan, waded ashore through the surf, and burned or drowned countless pirates.

sentences.zh: 是年夏，李長庚攻牽於鹿耳門，松年扼張坑、返埕洋面，獲賊船一，沉船三，又於水澳擒蔡三來等。

translations.literal: That summer Li Changgeng attacked Qian at Luer Gate; Songnian held Zhangkeng and Fancheng seas, captured one bandit ship, sank three, and at Shuiao captured Cai Sanlai and others.
translations.idiomatic: That summer Li Changgeng attacked Qian at Luer Gate while Songnian held Zhangkeng and Fancheng waters, captured one pirate ship, sank three, and at Shuiao took Cai Sanlai and others.

sentences.zh: 李長庚論水師將材，舉松年可獨當一面，總督阿林保以疏聞。

translations.literal: Li Changgeng discussed naval command talent and cited Songnian as able to hold an independent front; Governor Alinbao reported this in a memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Li Changgeng praised Songnian as capable of independent command, and Governor Alinbao reported this to court.

sentences.zh: 十二年，從長庚擊蔡牽於大星嶼、浮鷹洋，松年躍入賊船獲之，被優敘。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he followed Changgeng in attacking Cai Qian at Daxing Island and Fuying seas; Songnian leaped into a bandit ship and captured it, and received superior commendation.
translations.idiomatic: In 1807 he fought under Changgeng at Daxing Island and Fuying; Songnian boarded a pirate ship and captured it, earning superior commendation.

sentences.zh: 十三年，硃濆潛匿東涌外洋，命松年躡剿，遂移師入粵。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year Zhu Fen lay hidden in the outer seas off Dongyong; Songnian was ordered to track and suppress him and then moved his forces into Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: In 1808 Zhu Fen hid in the outer seas off Dongyong. Songnian was ordered to hunt him down and moved his forces into Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 追至長山尾，了見賊船四十餘，知其最巨者為濆所乘，並力圍攻，濆受砲傷，未幾斃。

translations.literal: Pursuing to Changshanwei, he clearly saw more than forty bandit ships and knew the largest was the one Fen rode; they united their strength to surround and attack; Fen was wounded by cannon and soon died.
translations.idiomatic: Pursuing to Changshanwei, he sighted more than forty pirate ships and identified the largest as Fen's. They surrounded it together; Fen was wounded by cannon fire and died shortly afterward.

sentences.zh: 詔嘉松年奮勇，克殲渠魁，賜花翎，予雲騎尉世職。

translations.literal: An edict praised Songnian's valor in destroying the ringleader, granted him the peacock feather, and gave him the hereditary office of Cloud Cavalry Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: An edict praised Songnian's valor in destroying the ringleader, awarded him the peacock feather, and granted him the hereditary office of Cloud Cavalry Commandant.

sentences.zh: 粵匪張保仔竄閩洋金門、廈門，松年遣漁船誘之，以舟師圍擊，獲船七，沉船六，被優敘。

translations.literal: The Cantonese bandit Zhang Baozi fled into the Fujian seas at Jinmen and Xiamen; Songnian sent fishing boats to lure him, surrounded and attacked with the fleet, captured seven ships, sank six, and received superior commendation.
translations.idiomatic: The Guangdong bandit Zhang Baozi raided Jinmen and Xiamen waters. Songnian used fishing boats as bait, surrounded him with the fleet, captured seven ships, sank six, and earned superior commendation.

sentences.zh: 十五年，傷發回籍，尋丁母憂。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year his wounds reopened and he returned to his native place; soon he entered mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: In 1810 his wounds reopened and he returned home; he soon entered mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 十九年，授甘肅西寧鎮總兵，歷延綏、漳州、天津、碣石諸鎮。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he was appointed regional commander of the Xining Garrison in Gansu and served in succession at the Yansui, Zhangzhou, Tianjin, and Jieshi garrisons.
translations.idiomatic: In 1814 he was appointed regional commander of the Xining Garrison in Gansu and later held commands at Yansui, Zhangzhou, Tianjin, and Jieshi.

sentences.zh: 道光元年，擢廣東陸路提督，調福建水師提督。

translations.literal: In the first year of Daoguang he was promoted to land commander-in-chief of Guangdong and transferred to naval commander-in-chief of Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: In 1821 he was promoted to land commander-in-chief of Guangdong and transferred to naval commander-in-chief of Fujian.

sentences.zh: 六年，台灣械鬥，松年方閱兵，彈壓解散，總督孫爾準與之不協，尋以治理輕縱，被議褫職，留台效力。

translations.literal: In the sixth year there was armed fighting in Taiwan; Songnian was inspecting troops and suppressed and dispersed it; Governor-General Sun Erzhun was at odds with him; soon he was criticized for lax governance, stripped of office, and kept in Taiwan to serve.
translations.idiomatic: In 1826 armed clashes broke out in Taiwan while Songnian was inspecting troops; he suppressed and dispersed them. Governor-General Sun Erzhun was at odds with him, and Songnian was soon criticized for lax governance, stripped of office, and kept in Taiwan to serve.

sentences.zh: 乞病歸，卒於家。

translations.literal: He begged leave on grounds of illness and returned home, and died at home.
translations.idiomatic: He retired on grounds of illness and died at home.

sentences.zh: 子錫麟，襲世職。

translations.literal: His son Xilin inherited the hereditary office.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xilin inherited the hereditary office.

sentences.zh: 黃標，字殿豪，廣東潮州人。

translations.literal: Huang Biao, courtesy name Dianhao, was a native of Chaozhou in Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Biao, whose courtesy name was Dianhao, came from Chaozhou in Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 由行伍拔補千總，擢守備。

translations.literal: From the ranks he was selected and made up as company commander and was promoted to garrison commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Selected from the ranks, he was made up as company commander and promoted to garrison commandant.

sentences.zh: 乾隆五十五年，艇匪肆掠，總督福康安議練水師，募奇才異能者領之。

translations.literal: In the fifty-fifth year of Qianlong, junk pirates plundered freely; Governor-General Fuk'anggan proposed training the navy and recruiting men of unusual talent and ability to lead it.
translations.idiomatic: In 1790 junk pirates raided freely. Governor-General Fuk'anggan proposed training the navy and recruiting men of exceptional ability to lead it.

sentences.zh: 標技勇過人，生長海壖，習知水道險易，能久伏水底，視物歷歷可數，特被識拔。

translations.literal: Biao's skill and courage surpassed others; he had grown up on the seashore, was practiced in the hazards and eases of waterways, could stay long submerged underwater and count objects clearly, and was specially recognized and promoted.
translations.idiomatic: Biao's skill and courage were extraordinary. Raised on the coast, he knew every channel's hazards and could stay submerged for long periods, counting objects underwater with perfect clarity. He was singled out for promotion.

sentences.zh: 以捕獲龍門洋盜及狗頭山匪功，擢都司，署游擊。

translations.literal: For merit in capturing pirates at Longmen seas and bandits at Goutou Mountain he was promoted to battalion commander and acted as battalion officer.
translations.idiomatic: For capturing pirates off Longmen and bandits at Goutou Mountain he was promoted to battalion commander and served in an acting capacity as battalion officer.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶元年，剿匪於南澎外洋，獲李超勝等三十餘名。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jiaqing he suppressed bandits in the outer seas off Nanpeng and captured more than thirty men including Li Chaosheng.
translations.idiomatic: In 1796 he suppressed bandits in the outer seas off Nanpeng and captured more than thirty men including Li Chaosheng.

sentences.zh: 仁宗素知其名，詔嘉緝捕勤能，擢參將。

translations.literal: Emperor Renzong had long known his name; an edict praised his diligence and ability in pursuit and capture and promoted him to brigade commander.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Renzong had long known his name. An edict praised his diligence in coastal defense and promoted him to brigade commander.

sentences.zh: 二年，俘洋盜胡三勝等，复擊斃安南匪首，盡獲其眾，被優敘。

translations.literal: In the second year he captured the foreign pirate Hu Sansheng and others, again attacked and killed the Annamese bandit chief, took all his followers, and received superior commendation.
translations.idiomatic: In 1797 he captured the foreign pirate Hu Sansheng and others, killed an Annamese bandit chief, took all his followers, and earned superior commendation.

sentences.zh: 三年，遷澄海副將。

translations.literal: In the third year he was transferred to deputy commander at Chenghai.
translations.idiomatic: In 1798 he was transferred to deputy commander at Chenghai.

sentences.zh: 未幾，擢廣東左翼鎮總兵，命總統巡洋水師，責以肅清海盜。

translations.literal: Before long he was promoted to regional commander of the Left Wing Garrison in Guangdong, ordered to take overall command of the coastal patrol navy, and charged with pacifying piracy.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to regional commander of the Left Wing Garrison in Guangdong, placed in overall command of coastal patrol forces, and charged with clearing the seas of pirates.

sentences.zh: 四年，剿匪大放雞山及雙魚桅、夾門外洋，殲獲甚眾，賜花翎，命繪像以進。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he suppressed bandits off Dafangji Mountain and at Shuangyuyan and Jiamen outer seas, destroyed and captured a great many, was granted the peacock feather, and ordered to have his portrait painted and presented.
translations.idiomatic: In 1799 he suppressed bandits off Dafangji Mountain, Shuangyuyan, and Jiamen outer seas, killed or captured a great many, was awarded the peacock feather, and ordered to have his portrait presented to court.

sentences.zh: 尋以盜劫鹽艘被劾，詔原之。

translations.literal: Soon he was impeached because bandits had robbed salt transport ships; an edict pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon impeached after pirates robbed salt transport ships under his watch, but an edict pardoned him.

sentences.zh: 六年，复擊賊於南澎外洋，獲田亞猛等。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he again attacked bandits in the outer seas off Nanpeng and captured Tian Yameng and others.
translations.idiomatic: In 1801 he again fought pirates in the outer seas off Nanpeng and captured Tian Yameng and others.

sentences.zh: 七年，偕提督孫全謀剿博羅會匪，連破羊矢坑、羅溪營要隘，搗其巢。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, together with Commander-in-Chief Sun Quanmou, he suppressed the Boluo secret-society bandits, repeatedly broke the passes at Yangshikeng and Luoxi Camp, and destroyed their nest.
translations.idiomatic: In 1802 he joined Commander-in-Chief Sun Quanmou in suppressing the Boluo secret-society rebels, broke the passes at Yangshikeng and Luoxi Camp in succession, and destroyed their stronghold.

sentences.zh: 事平優敘，並被珍賚。

translations.literal: When the affair was pacified he received superior commendation and was also given rare gifts.
translations.idiomatic: When the campaign ended he received superior commendation and rare gifts from the throne.

sentences.zh: 自將水師，飲食寢處與士卒共，先後獲匪六百餘名，粵海倚為保障。

translations.literal: He personally commanded the navy, sharing food, drink, and sleeping quarters with the soldiers; before and after he captured more than six hundred bandits, and the Guangdong seas relied on him as their safeguard.
translations.idiomatic: He commanded the navy in person, sharing food and quarters with his men. He captured more than six hundred bandits in all, and the Guangdong coast came to rely on him as its main defense.

sentences.zh: 八年，偕孫全謀出海捕賊，賊遁廣州灣。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he went to sea with Sun Quanmou to capture bandits; the bandits fled into Guangzhou Bay.
translations.idiomatic: In 1803 he went to sea with Sun Quanmou to hunt pirates, who fled into Guangzhou Bay.

sentences.zh: 標議合兵守隘，俟賊糧盡可盡殲。

translations.literal: Biao proposed uniting the armies to hold the passes and wait until the bandits' provisions were exhausted so they could be wholly destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Biao proposed concentrating forces to block the passes and wait until the pirates' provisions ran out so they could be destroyed entirely.

sentences.zh: 全謀慮持久有風濤患，乃分兵，賊得突圍逸出。

translations.literal: Quanmou feared that a prolonged stand would bring wind and wave troubles, so he divided the troops, and the bandits were able to break out and escape.
translations.idiomatic: Quanmou feared a prolonged blockade would expose the fleet to storms and divided his forces, allowing the pirates to break out and escape.

sentences.zh: 標歎曰：「此機一失，海警未已！

translations.literal: Biao sighed and said: "Once this chance is lost, maritime alarms will not end!"
translations.idiomatic: Biao sighed and said, "Once this chance is lost, the coast will never know peace!"

sentences.zh: 」憤懣成疾。

translations.literal: " Anger and distress turned into illness.
translations.idiomatic: " Grief and anger brought on illness.

sentences.zh: 尋坐師久無功，吏議奪職留任。

translations.literal: Soon he was charged with commanding troops long without success; the civil officials proposed stripping his office while keeping him on duty.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon charged with commanding troops for too long without success; the civil officials proposed stripping his rank while keeping him on duty.

sentences.zh: 未幾，卒。

translations.literal: Before long he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died shortly afterward.

sentences.zh: 自安南夷艇散後，餘黨留粵者分五幫：曰林阿發、曰總兵保、曰郭學顯、曰烏石二、曰鄭乙。

translations.literal: After the Annamese foreign junks dispersed, the remaining followers who stayed in Guangdong divided into five gangs: those of Lin Afa, Zongbing Bao, Guo Xuexian, Wushi Er, and Zheng Yi.
translations.idiomatic: After the Annamese pirate junks dispersed, the remnants in Guangdong split into five gangs led by Lin Afa, Zongbing Bao, Guo Xuexian, Wushi Er, and Zheng Yi.

sentences.zh: 提督錢夢虎、孫全謀皆庸材，不能辦賊。

translations.literal: Commanders-in-Chief Qian Menghu and Sun Quanmou were both mediocre talents and could not deal with the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Commanders-in-Chief Qian Menghu and Sun Quanmou were both mediocre and unable to suppress the pirates.

sentences.zh: 標歿後，益無良將，惟林國良、許廷桂以死事聞。

translations.literal: After Biao died there were even fewer good generals; only Lin Guoliang and Xu Tinggui were known for dying in service.
translations.idiomatic: After Biao's death there were even fewer capable commanders; only Lin Guoliang and Xu Tinggui were remembered for dying in battle.

sentences.zh: 國良，福建海澄人。

translations.literal: Guoliang was a native of Haicheng in Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: Guoliang came from Haicheng in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 世襲騎都尉，授廣東碣石鎮標游擊，累遷海澄副將，繼標為左翼鎮總兵。

translations.literal: He inherited the office of Cavalry Commandant, was appointed battalion officer of the Jieshi Garrison standard in Guangdong, was repeatedly promoted to deputy commander at Haicheng, and succeeded Biao as regional commander of the Left Wing Garrison.
translations.idiomatic: He inherited the office of Cavalry Commandant, served as battalion officer of the Jieshi Garrison standard in Guangdong, rose to deputy commander at Haicheng, and succeeded Biao as regional commander of the Left Wing Garrison.

sentences.zh: 十三年，追剿烏石二於丫洲洋，擊沉數艘，賊艦續至益多。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he pursued and suppressed Wushi Er at Yazhou seas, sank several ships, and bandit vessels continued arriving in ever greater numbers.
translations.idiomatic: In 1808 he pursued Wushi Er off Yazhou, sank several ships, and ever more pirate vessels kept arriving.

sentences.zh: 國良以傷殞，優恤，諡果壯。

translations.literal: Guoliang died of his wounds; he received generous condolence rewards and was given the posthumous title Resolute and Robust.
